book.slavicmyths.intro.title: First traces
book.slavicmyths.intro.text:
Old tales live beneath the familiar world. Craft this book from a book, birch bark scroll and linen thread.

Interact with spirits to learn about them. An ancient coin or fragment reveals the shrine entry; touching an idol also works. Use an altar to learn the rite. Completing it reveals its tale.

Scroll: two birch bark and string. Charm: linen thread, wormwood and a gold nugget. Standard recipes appear in the recipe book and JEI.
book.slavicmyths.domovoy.title: Spirits: Domovoy
book.slavicmyths.domovoy.text:
A small guardian values a peaceful home. Bread, milk, honey and cookies build trust, with a minute between gifts. Four gifts earn friendship. Attacks cause resentment; repeated blows hurt trust more. An angry spirit refuses food.

Build a hearth from a campfire, four cobblestone and four birch bark. Use it with a friend nearby to bind a home. Another player cannot claim your guardian. Eight gifts earn devotion: ask with an empty hand near home for five seconds of regeneration, once per ten minutes.

Inspired by folklore; trust rules are a game interpretation.
book.slavicmyths.leshy.title: Spirits: Leshy
book.slavicmyths.leshy.text:
The forest may speak before its guardian appears. By day the Leshy avoids travellers; do not approach too closely at night. Avoid needless violence.

Its blows sometimes slow you for three seconds. A wounded guardian may vanish nearby, at most once in thirty seconds. Its heart is rare loot, not a required cost of the first rite.

These abilities are game interpretations, not a claim of a single folklore canon.
book.slavicmyths.shrine.title: Places: shrine
book.slavicmyths.shrine.text:
A broken stone circle, an old tree and a nameless idol. Rarely found on flat ground in Overworld plains, forests and taiga, in newly generated chunks.

A chest holds remnants of offerings: herbs, bark, coins and fragments. The altar can be taken home. The idol is not yet dedicated to a specific deity.

This place is a game design, not a historical reconstruction.
book.slavicmyths.altar.title: Rites: altar
book.slavicmyths.altar.text:
Right-click to offer one item at a time. The first rite requires wormwood, a birch bark scroll, then a warding charm. Wrong items are not consumed. An empty hand reveals the next step.

Progress survives world reloads. Altars are shared: another player may continue the rite. The finisher receives the sign. Breaking the altar cancels progress; committed offerings are not returned. A completed rite can be repeated immediately.
book.slavicmyths.ritual.title: Rites: first sign
book.slavicmyths.ritual.text:
Bitter herbs, the memory of bark, the knot of a charm. Three offerings unite in an Ancient Sign. It marks a first step into old knowledge and grants no combat power yet.

This rite is an original game interpretation. Keep coins and fragments for future tales: trading and further rites are not implemented yet.
book.slavicmyths.paths.title: Paths
book.slavicmyths.paths.text: Paths are a game system, not a historical classification. Find a small shrine in new plains or forest chunks, or craft a Path Stone. Initiation costs 10 levels and two offerings; the choice is permanent. Buy skills with vanilla levels; later skills need discoveries. After three skills choose one secondary path, limited to its first three skills. Select an active ability with G at the stone, then press G in the world. Progress survives death.

book.slavicmyths.runes.title: Runes
book.slavicmyths.runes.text: Runes are fictional Slavic Myths signs, not historical canon. Offer in order at the altar: Thunder — thunder stone, perunite, ancient sign; Heat — ritual charcoal, ember heart, sign; Forest — Leshy heart, wormwood, sign; Midday — noon ear, silver, sign; Shadow — Kikimora lock, silver, sign; Protection — silver, warding charm, sign; Life — fern flower, honey bottle, sign; Wind — feather, fireweed, sign. Recipes are also visible in JEI. Runes require no class.
book.slavicmyths.reforging.title: Reforging
book.slavicmyths.reforging.text: At a Runic Anvil put the weapon in slot one, material in slot two, catalyst in slot three. First socket: 3 iron and 6 levels. Second: 2 silver, an ancient sign, 15 levels. Third: 3 perunite, an Ovinnik claw, 28 levels. Caps: wood and stone 1; iron and silver 2; perunite and diamond 3. Installing costs 7 levels and a rune; removal costs 2 levels and destroys the rune. No duplicate runes. Take the result from slot one; closing returns all items. Vanilla enchantments, name and durability are preserved.

book.slavicmyths.water_fish.title: River life
book.slavicmyths.water_fish.text: Pike are long ambush fish, carp are broad and calm, crayfish live near the bottom. Freshwater catches supplement the normal rod. Oceans retain vanilla fish. Smoke carp; cook ukha at the kitchen table using cooked pike, potato, bowl and a pot.
book.slavicmyths.fishing_net.title: Fishing net
book.slavicmyths.fishing_net.text: Place a net in water near the bottom. Every 5–7 minutes it attempts a catch, up to four stored fish. Use to collect; sneak-use to retrieve. After 32 catches it breaks. Crowded nets are less efficient; use a rod for treasure.
book.slavicmyths.vodyanoy.title: Vodyanoy
book.slavicmyths.vodyanoy.text: Vodyanoy rules local water. Bread, karavai and nacre improve relations. Overfishing and crowded nets anger him. A friendly master grants fishing luck; an angry one is dangerous underwater. This is a gameplay interpretation of folklore.
book.slavicmyths.rusalka.title: Rusalka
book.slavicmyths.rusalka.text: Do not linger when you hear her song. A warning grows into a pull toward the water. Leave the 20-block range, take cover, or interrupt her with a hit. Gusli and the Veles amulet reduce exposure without granting immunity. Charm fades quickly after escape. This human-shaped, tailless spirit is a gameplay interpretation of Slavic folklore.

book.slavicmyths.elder_vodyanoy.title: Elder Vodyanoy
book.slavicmyths.elder_vodyanoy.text: Vodyanoy is a folkloric water spirit. The Elder is an original gameplay interpretation of a very old spirit, not a separate documented mythological figure. Earn a sign through offerings or find one rarely while fishing in rivers and swamps.
book.slavicmyths.deep_pool.title: The Elder’s pool
book.slavicmyths.deep_pool.text: Look for old posts and a dark depression in newly generated river and swamp chunks. The sign points toward a pool already loaded by the world; it does not generate distant chunks. Use it on the central stone. Bubbles warn of the encounter. High wooden ledges remain dry.
book.slavicmyths.pool_pearl.title: Pearl of the Pool
book.slavicmyths.pool_pearl.text: Victory guarantees three pearls, enough for spear, amulet and net. A defeated pool does not respawn its master after reloading. This is a rare material, not a complete equipment tier.
book.slavicmyths.pool_spear.title: Pool spear
book.slavicmyths.pool_spear.text: On land it is a slow, strong spear. In water, hold use for at least 0.8 seconds and release for a short thrust: up to 9 damage to a nearby target ahead, six-second cooldown and durability cost. Movement respects walls.
book.slavicmyths.depth_amulet.title: Depth amulet
book.slavicmyths.depth_amulet.text: Curios necklace slot. Extends normal air supply by roughly one third without granting endless breathing. Reduces Rusalka pull by 30% and weakens the Elder’s pull. The Vodyanoy net briefly slows ordinary targets, more strongly in water; bosses are immune.
depth.slavicmyths.hint.unknown: The sign is quiet. Explore deep rivers and swamps.
depth.slavicmyths.hint.near: An old power rests in nearby water.
book.slavicmyths.swamp_hut.title: Swamp hut
book.slavicmyths.swamp_hut.text: An old human log house stands above damp soil. Stove and vestibule recall its inhabitants. Water may collect beneath damaged roofing; inspect the remaining household corners. This is a game reconstruction, not an exact historical building.
book.slavicmyths.abandoned_settlement.te: A well connects the yard, houses and barn. One house survived better; another slowly sank. Paths show how people lived here, while the way out disappears into the bog. Abandoned does not necessarily mean occupied by hostile spirits.
book.slavicmyths.bog_causeway.title: Old causeway
book.slavicmyths.bog_causeway.text: Longitudinal logs support the old walkway. The causeway still crosses wet ground despite sunken planks. A broken branch may once have led to people.
book.slavicmyths.flooded_shrine.title: Beneath black water
book.slavicmyths.flooded_shrine.text: Broken posts outline an ancient platform. Its weathered central stone needs no ritual. Inspect its underwater edges: a small space remains beneath the stonework. This shrine is an original game interpretation, not a claim about a specific Slavic rite.
book.slavicmyths.fishing_camp.title: Fishing camp
book.slavicmyths.fishing_camp.text: The canopy, barrels and work surface belonged to fishers. The pier remains recognizable, but its end is broken. A wooden boat hull rests underwater nearby. Look for remnants of the old fishing trade.
book.slavicmyths.underwater_ruins.title: What rests below
book.slavicmyths.underwater_ruins.text: Foundations and beams below may belong to a home, warehouse or old landing. Remember the way to the surface before diving. Food and a Depth Amulet help prepare, but air is still limited.
advancement.slavicmyths.bog_explorer.des: Visit all six major wetland structure categories

book.slavicmyths.bandit_gangs.text: Bandits are humans, not spirits. Fighters telegraph strikes and recover. Archers keep their distance; heavies briefly raise shields. Look for camps in plains, forests and taiga. These characters are game interpretations.
book.slavicmyths.bandit_small.title: Small camp
book.slavicmyths.bandit_small.text: Low canvas tents, a fire and supplies mark a temporary camp. The senior wears better equipment but is not a boss. Most rewards are stored in camp.
book.slavicmyths.bandit_medium.title: Fortified camp
book.slavicmyths.bandit_medium.text: A warehouse, lookout and palisade fragments protect a larger gang. One Ataman leads a fixed roster of nine including himself. Defeat every member to clear it; chunk unloading does not replenish defenders.
book.slavicmyths.ataman.title: Ataman
book.slavicmyths.ataman.text: A human in good armor. Watch for the long heavy-strike wind-up and short shield phases. His commands help nearby bandits maintain their target. His death ends that assistance.
book.slavicmyths.arms_craft.title: Arms craft
book.slavicmyths.arms_craft.text: Craft the armorer table from three iron ingots, four spruce planks and a crafting table. Its 4×4 grid uses separate recipes, shown by optional JEI. One ingot makes two sets of rings. Arrange rings as chainmail armor. Maces are slower than swords, knock targets back and pressure armor. Hold flail use for 0.9 seconds, then release for a strike up to four blocks, followed by a two-second cooldown. Gambeson provides 4 armor; the cuirass provides 7 with a 5% movement penalty.

book.slavicmyths.woodlands.title: Trees of the Homeland
book.slavicmyths.woodlands.text: Linden spreads a broad crown above pale timber. Small rowans grow among other trees; pick their berry clusters by hand. Berries slowly regrow on living leaves near branches. Willows favour banks, trailing narrow leaves over water. Pines raise uneven needle boughs above an open trunk. All four timbers make planks, doors, fences and signs. Plant a sapling on soil and encourage it with bone meal.
book.slavicmyths.forest_whistle.title: A Whistle in the Thicket
book.slavicmyths.forest_whistle.text: Even the atamans do not rule these roads. When a whistle carries over the forest, fires are put out and people shelter behind thick walls. Deep inside the settlement an old tree bears an empty platform. Dark feathers catch between its boards, and heavy targets are split as though struck by a whole trunk.

book.slavicmyths.nightingale.title: Nightingale the Robber
book.slavicmyths.nightingale.text: The feather in the bandit stronghold was a taunt, not a bird omen. Above the yard, beside an old pine, sits a broad-shouldered man with a heavy dagger. He does not sing: first he falls silent, opens his chest and draws in enough air to stir the dust. Seek a thick trunk or a boulder then; a flimsy fence will not shelter you. Rush straight to his platform and the surviving gang may follow at your heels. A dark token hangs from his belt. Craftsmen bind a lock of his hair into a bone whistle. After his final broken whistle, the road falls quiet at last.

wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.offered: I promised to tell you of one final trouble. A Cursed Werewolf roams the woods, a beast whose fury neither steel nor fire can quell. Once he was a man; now a curse binds him tighter than chains. My strength is no longer what it was. Find him and stop him.

wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.accepted.3: The last trail leads deep into the forest, %s. Search roughly near X≈%s, Z≈%s, but remember: the beast will not wait in one clearing.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.active: Birds fall silent where the Cursed Werewolf passes, and animals avoid those paths. Seek the disturbed silence among the trees.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.track: Birds fall silent where the Cursed Werewolf passes, and animals avoid those paths. Seek the disturbed silence among the trees.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.fight: You have found his trail. Beware his claws and jaws: his blood carries misfortune. If the forest does not grow quiet after the fight, the curse still lives.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.find_curs: I feared this. The beast does not hold the curse; the curse holds the beast. Forgotten human remains lie nearby, never laid peacefully to rest. Weeping herb grows above that grave. Find it and recover the hidden skull.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.excavate: Look for pale flowers and darkened earth. Not every grave has a stone, but the soil remembers forgotten sorrow.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.return: You found the unburied skull. Bring it to the Grey Wolf; only he knows how to quiet the spirit.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.handed.3: Here it is, the sign of an old misfortune. This man knew no rest for many years, and grief made him a savage beast. You defeated the Cursed Werewolf and found the cause of his torment. The earth will accept its burden and the curse shall end. I will remember your kindness, traveller. As promised, take Finist's Bow and Quiver, gifts from my long life.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.reward_re: Take Finist's Bow and Quiver. May their arrows help where even claws fail. Our work is done for now, but our paths will meet again.
wolfstory.slavicmyths.dialog.3.completed: The forest remembers those who did not turn away from another's sorrow. Go in peace, my friend.

book.slavicmyths.industry.text: Bog iron occurs beneath swamp ground and requires a stone pickaxe. The Chud Bloomery turns one lump into one iron ingot in 10 seconds. The Refining Hearth consumes an iron or copper ingot, one flux and fuel to produce a purified ingot in 15 seconds. Chud artisans and smelters sell flux. Purified metals make goggles, a ring, an amulet and a belt. Goggles occupy the Curios head slot and grant Night Vision. Smelters sell mining runes; install them in pickaxe sockets at the existing Runic Anvil. Mining runes improve ore mining speed; the fortune rune adds one effective Fortune level up to IV without rewriting enchantments, with Silk Touch taking priority. Rare residents sell finished accessories, and new Chud structures contain themed chests. This is a game interpretation, not a historical description of metallurgy.

tales.entry.kot_bayun.rumor: A large grey cat with amber eyes lives at an old forest stump. The fairy-tale Bayun lulls travellers with speech; this encounter turns that image into a warning, a song and a physical pounce. Force cannot defeat him. Prepare milk or raw fish and keep an escape route.
tales.entry.kot_bayun.discovered: He notices travellers within 12 blocks. An eight-second grace period is followed by a three-and-a-half-second warning. The song reaches 15 blocks and may charm after two seconds. A wall or timely retreat interrupts the encounter. Do not wait next to him.
tales.entry.kot_bayun.studied:
Within three blocks offer a milk bucket, raw cod or salmon. Milk returns an empty bucket. The first gift adds 15 trust, plus 10 for milk or 8 for fish. Gifts have a one-day cooldown. Safe sneak-interaction within 2.5 blocks adds four trust every two days. Each traveller has a separate bond.

Current default attributes: health 100 HP, armour 0. Evaluate changes of state during the actual encounter.
tales.entry.kot_bayun.verified:
Friendship begins at 85 trust and persists for your UUID in this world. An accepted gift also makes the meeting safe. Four dialogue choices offer a tale, an introduction, an honest hint to his own home or goodbye. The map shows an approximate area, not exact coordinates. Friendship is not a victory over the cat.
